claim: For three independent uses of the pentagon confusability channel, equivalently the strong graph power \(C_5^{\boxtimes 3}\), the maximum zero-error code size is \(10\). Exactly \(391{,}600\) maximum codes of size \(10\) exist on the labeled alphabet \((\mathbb Z/5\mathbb Z)^3\), and exactly \(31{,}328\) contain any prescribed word. Under the natural channel-isometry group \(G=(D_{10})^3\rtimes S_3\) of order \(6000\), the maxima form exactly \(85\) orbits. Their stabilizer-order distribution is \(1^{53},2^{19},3^2,4^7,8^1,10^2,40^1\). The unique orbit with stabilizer order \(40\) has representative \(\{(0,0,0),(0,0,2),(1,2,0),(1,2,2),(2,4,0),(2,4,2),(3,1,0),(3,1,2),(4,3,0),(4,3,2)\}\).

correctness.rationale: The packaged verifier reconstructs the compatibility graph directly from cyclic distance, exhaustively proves that no size-11 code containing a fixed word exists, enumerates all 31,328 size-10 codes containing that word, directly rechecks every pair in every enumerated code, double-counts to 391,600 labeled maxima, canonicalizes them under the stated natural group, and independently recomputes all 85 stabilizers. The orbit-size sum exactly equals the independent incidence count. Risk is implementation error; it is mitigated by these redundant defining-condition and counting checks, but no independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The pentagon channel is the canonical finite example in zero-error information theory where block coding and strong graph products are central. Classifying every three-use optimum is therefore a natural equality problem, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The result shows a large and highly non-rigid equality landscape—85 natural symmetry types—behind the classical scalar optimum 10, supplies exact labeled and fixed-word counts, and gives a reproducible finite benchmark for structural work on zero-error codes and strong powers. Risk: it is a finite result and does not by itself improve Shannon-capacity bounds.
